text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen favourably disposed towards NATO offer of enhanced Partnership for Peace. Says Finland sees NATO as a partner in maintaining stability in northern Europe.
- Car dealers in southern Uusimaa province have sold 65 million markka worth of cars off the books, police and tax officials found.

- Consortium of local telephone companies Finnet-liitto unable to agree on model for forming a joint company at this stage. Major player Helsinki Telephone Company (HPY) wanted a tighter organisation than regional operators.
- Two new professorships for women's studies to be established next year.
- Sweden has highest tax rate in the EU, Eurostat says.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finnish banks likely to lose up to a billion markka annually in income and another billion in technical costs if Europe adopts a common currency.
- Owners of Finnyards have paid 200 million markka of the corporation's two-year losses to enable it start business with a clean slate.
- Licensing conditions for the fourth commercial television channel approved by the government distort competition, says MTV Oy executive Jaakko Paavela.
AAMULEHTI
- Credit-worthiness of Finnish companies has improved. Dun & Bradstreet gives at least an "A" rating to about 60 percent of Finnish firms and a "C" to only about five percent.
- Elk hunting season begins on Saturday. This year's bag is expected to be lowest in years.
- Newly licenced nationwide television channel plans to grab 15 percent of Finnish TV viewers.
- Finland's small Jewish community broadly connected with the mainstream Finnish culture -- total assimilation a threat.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finnish coastal artillery breaks 50-year old "gentlemen's agreement" and opens fire over civilian area in exercises.
- Stuntman says he can't tell his grandparents what he does for a living.
--Helsinki Newsroom +358-0-680 50 235
